label: March 1918
headline: Arras Holds
deck: A second blow at the British line fails; Moscow becomes the capital
caption: British gunners fire over open sights as grey lines advance east of Arras
body: On 28 March, a week after the great offensive on the Somme, the Germans strike again at Arras, further north. This time the British front is fully manned, its defences deep, and the morning clear: the attack breaks down on the first day with heavy losses, and the hinge of the line holds.
In Russia the government leaves Petrograd, now within reach of German troops, and on 12 March moves to Moscow, which becomes the capital once more, for the first time since Peter the Great.
In Ukraine German and Austro-Hungarian troops occupy Kiev and Odessa under the treaty with the Rada, and grain trains begin to roll west to the hungry cities of Germany and Austria.
At Murmansk, on 6 March, a small party of British marines lands to guard Allied stores.
briefs: Romania signs a preliminary peace with the Central Powers at Buftea
In Palestine the British cross the Jordan and raid Amman
